subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The International Space Station: Built in Orbit
description: Learn The International Space Station: Built in Orbit in one minute.

hook.text: The ISS was assembled in orbit from 42 separate launches over 13 years. No crane. No ground. Just astronauts and robotic arms.

buildup.text: Each module was designed by different countries in different languages. Every connection had to fit perfectly on the first try.

discovery.text: The truss spans 357 feet — longer than a football field. It holds the solar panels and radiators that power and cool the station.

twist.text: The station orbits in near-vacuum but isn't truly empty. It drags through enough atmosphere to lose altitude and needs reboosts.

climax.text: The ISS has been continuously inhabited since November 2000. It's the longest continuous human presence in space in history.

punchline.text: 42 launches. 16 nations. Assembled in zero gravity. Our home in orbit.

quiz.question: Why does the ISS need regular reboosts to maintain its orbit?
options: The Moon's gravity gradually pulls it into a higher, less useful orbit
Residual atmospheric drag slowly lowers its altitude over time
Solar wind pressure pushes it further from Earth each month
